description: [roadmap S3.1b] The generic GL's specular term is a table of 256 entries over [t, 1], t = 0.0005^(1 / shininess), read at the NEAREST entry without interpolation (i = round((n.h - t) * 255 / (1 - t)), value (t + i * (1 - t) / 255)^shininess, 0 for n.h <= t). Measured with untextured constant-colour quads through re/tools/glexact/glreplay.exe (port/test/glprobe.py untex, log/roadmap/S3/1b_litfit.py): 0 of 4,923 quads outside the interval their 16 dither cells allow (white specular only, four seeds), against 793 for the exact pow; every pixel equal at shininess 1, 5, 13, 40 and 128. Not determined: whether the index and the table are evaluated in float32 or double (both give 0 violations), and the behaviour with a positional light or a local viewer (the terrain uses neither: a directional light 0, viewer at infinity). | A probe with a positional light / GL_LIGHT_MODEL_LOCAL_VIEWER, only if a future caller sets them. | open

[roadmap S3.1b] Pixel centres exactly on an edge: the rule `an edge owns them when it points to +y, or to +x when horizontal` (spans: ymin <= y + 0.5 < ymax, xl < x + 0.5 <= xr) is the best of the six simple rules on the tie probe (port/test/glprobe.py tie: 48 coverage differences of about 4,600 pixels against 288 .. 923), and it takes g6/i005_raised_pathupd from 145 to 10 pixels more than one level off. The 48 left are centres exactly on a vertex (40) or on a diagonal edge (8), where the real GL's choice follows no direction rule (both signs occur for the same edge direction): a fixed-point edge walker's rounding, not modelled. In the recorded corpora such pixels are what is left of the pixels more than one level off (at most 13 per pass, c7 fuzz frames). | A probe of the real GL with one triangle per scene and its vertex moved along the 1/256 grid around a centre, to read the edge walker's start and step arithmetic. | open

[roadmap S3.1b] What is left of the one-level noise after U-1390 / U-1391 is 0.0 .. 0.21 % of the drawn pixels per pass on every recorded pass (c3 .. c7, t3, g2 .. g6; mean 0.03 .. 0.06 % per corpus), down from 0.33 .. 0.49 % (1.21 % on g6); its origin was not split further. Section 18's `per-triangle constant shift would still remove about 70 %` measurement (U-1076) was taken with the exact pow, whose error is constant per flat-normal triangle, so that residual needs re-measuring with the table before it is attributed to the setup. | Re-run section 18's per-triangle fit (sg_raster_get_tri_ids) on t3 / c7 with the table and the tie rule. | open
